## HISTORY AND PHYSICAL
Date of Service: 10/05/2026 00:30
Attending: Esther Mwangi, MD (Hospital Medicine)
## HPI
35 y/o M with schizophrenia, unhoused x 3 years, brought by police after found with a laceration to the L shin from climbing a fence. Laceration irrigated and closed in ED with 9 sutures. Pt reports he stopped his medications "a few months ago". Admitted to observation for wound care and psychiatric evaluation.
## PMH
- Schizophrenia (dx age 22), prior psychiatric hospitalizations x 3
## Social
Unhoused x 3 years. Smokes 1 ppd. Denies alcohol. Cannabis daily.
## Allergies

L anterior shin: 7 cm linear laceration closed with 9 sutures, edges approximated, no erythema.
Neuro: nonfocal. Alert, oriented to person and place only.
Psych: guarded, responding to internal stimuli
## Plan
1. Laceration - daily dressing, suture removal in 10-14 days; Tdap given
2. Psychiatry consult
Isolation: None - standard precautions

pages.title: Psychiatry consultation
pages.text:
## PSYCHIATRY CONSULTATION
Date: 10/05/2026 14:00
Consultant: H. Lindgren, MD (Psychiatry)
Reason: schizophrenia off medications, responding to internal stimuli
## Interview
Pt endorses hearing voices for several weeks. Reports command auditory hallucinations telling him to "go out and hide from the cameras" and to "not trust anyone who gives you pills".
Denies suicidal ideation. Denies homicidal ideation. Denies visual hallucinations.
Off risperidone for about 4 months. Declines to restart antipsychotic today.
## MSE
Disheveled, guarded, poor eye contact. Thought process: tangential. Thought content: paranoid delusions about surveillance. Perception: active command auditory hallucinations. Insight poor, judgment impaired.
Oriented to person and place, not to date.
## Assessment
Schizophrenia, acute exacerbation, nonadherent to medications. Does not currently meet 5150 criteria.
## Recommendations
- Encourage restart of risperidone; patient declining
- Referral to county outpatient mental health
- Not psychiatrically stable at this time
Signed: H. Lindgren, MD
